- **Marker:** 2026-11-20-browser-s-surviving-mutants · **Version:** escher-0.4.0

The 0.3.0 Epoch 6 boundary audit left four browser mutants missed. All four sit at `apps/browser/src/capture.rs:86:5` (`replace render_scene -> (u32, u32)` with `(0, 0)`, `(0, 1)`, `(1, 0)`, `(1, 1)`; metric `met-mjjioowg`, sha `bc766124`). The coordinate still stands at HEAD `80c31730e`: `render_scene` is declared at 81, and 86:5 is its body's first statement (scope; research §Patterns). Both callers discard the returned size (`render_scene @ capture.rs:48` in `capture_screenshot`, `@ capture.rs:70` in `capture_anyrender_scene`; research §Graph impact). So only a test that calls `render_scene` itself can tell the real size from the four constants.

This chunk catches the four with such a test: a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` appended at the end of `capture.rs`, upstream's code above it unchanged. The test builds two documents with literal viewports, 800 × 600 at scale 1.0 and 1280 × 720 at scale 2.0. It paints each through `render_scene` into anyrender's own no-op painter and asserts the returned size as literals: `(800, 600)` and `(1280, 720)`. This tests the directive's hypothesis (inputs#I1) as an equality. For `RenderSize::Viewport` the returned size is `Viewport::window_size`, the `(w, h)` given to `Viewport::new`, whatever the scale (research §Premise closure). Each constant is ≤ 1 in both dimensions, so each input alone already fails all four. The second input also pins that the size is physical, not divided by the scale. The test follows the project's unit-test conventions: inline at the file's end (architecture · decision/unit-tests-at-file-end; test-plan · decision/inline-cfg-test-modules), the test-document setup (architecture · decision/test-document-setup), literal expectations (test-plan · decision/expected-value-pinned-as-literal) and a control red before green (test-plan · decision/mutation-controlled-tests).

Under the mutation tier's own recipe (test-plan · decision/mutation-testing-dev-host-only, decision/mutation-runs-under-nextest-profile, decision/mutation-baseline-skipped), the cargo-mutants re-run of the four is an operator entry. The operator pass fires it only on the founder's word (inputs#I1), never by itself. Without that word the four read caught by the hand controls of acceptance 2, and the re-run stays owed to his word or to the next boundary audit.

1. Append a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of `apps/browser/src/capture.rs`, after `try_get_save_path`, editing nothing above it. It imports from `super` and builds each document as `tests/blitz-tests/tests/device_coalescing.rs:23-32` does: `blitz_html::HtmlDocument::from_html` over a small inline HTML page, with `DocumentConfig { viewport: Some(Viewport::new(w, h, scale, ColorScheme::Light)), html_parser_provider: Some(Arc::new(HtmlProvider) as _), ..Default::default() }`, so the default UA sheet comes through the config (design-system · decision/default-ua-sheet-via-default-config). Then it calls `resolve(0.0)` on the document. Every crate it names is already a browser dependency (`blitz-html`, `blitz-dom`, `blitz-traits`, `anyrender`; research §Files inspected), so `apps/browser/Cargo.toml` is not edited. Keeps tests S1–S4, arch S1–S4, obs S1, security S1–S2.

2. In that module, write two `#[test]` functions with descriptive names, each with a literal viewport and a literal expectation, asserting with `assert_eq!` (test-plan · decision/rust-tests-on-built-in-harness):
   - `render_scene_returns_the_viewport_size`: viewport 800 × 600 at scale 1.0. It first asserts the fixture: the document's `viewport().window_size` reads `(800, 600)` (architecture · decision/fixture-precondition-first). It then calls `render_scene(&mut doc, &mut anyrender::NullScenePainter, RenderSize::Viewport)` and asserts it returns `(800, 600)`.
   - `render_scene_returns_the_physical_size_at_a_hidpi_scale`: viewport 1280 × 720 at scale 2.0. The fixture check reads `(1280, 720)` and `scale_f64()` reads `2.0`; then `render_scene` returns `(1280, 720)`.
   No expected value is computed from the viewport the test sets. `anyrender::NullScenePainter` is the library's own no-op `PaintScene` (anyrender 0.15, `null_backend.rs:89`), so no hand-written stand-in is added (test-plan · decision/hand-written-stand-ins). An `expect` or `unwrap` in the module sits under a local `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` / `unwrap_used` next to a written justification (architecture · decision/justified-expect-unwrap). The tests print nothing and install no sink (obs-plan · decision/checks-silent).

3. Run the entries below in order. Then run the four hand controls once through `gate.py control` (§Test Commands prose), each writing one constant into `render_scene`'s returned tuple in the tool's clone. Both cases must read `failed` under each, and the restored tree reads green.

No smoke or boot leg runs this chunk. `capture.rs` is no boot-path file: the capture module runs only from the toolbar's screenshot and scene-capture buttons (`toolbar.rs:239`, `:262`), never at start-up, and the change adds test code alone. The project's mutation tier is not a CI leg (test-plan · decision/mutation-runs-on-dev-host-only). Its re-run here is entries 9 and 10, operator entries fired only on the founder's word.

The hand controls are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` run against entry 1, fired as itself. There are four `[[control]]`s, `id` `c00` · `c01` · `c10` · `c11`. Each has one `[[control.edit]]` in `apps/browser/src/capture.rs` with `old = '''    (render_width, render_height)
}'''` (it stands once, at capture.rs:99-100: the tuple and the function's closing brace) and `new` the same with `(0, 0)` · `(0, 1)` · `(1, 0)` · `(1, 1)`. Each control's `guard` is «render_scene's real returned size». Its `case` is `["render_scene_returns_the_viewport_size", "render_scene_returns_the_physical_size_at_a_hidpi_scale"]`, the libtest names' last segment. libtest runs every filtered test with no fail-fast, so both cases are reached. The kill is the default 1 800 s, since entry 1 declares `timeout = 1800`, sized to a cold per-package build of the browser. A `timeout` reading is not read as the guard held. The tool must print `control: 4 holds`. The readings go to `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-20-browser-s-surviving-mutants/evidence/controls.md`.
A per-package green is not the workspace green (test-plan · decision/per-package-green-not-workspace-green), so entry 2 runs the local pre-push gate over the workspace.
